newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelans sign historic severance pay agreement.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelans sign historic severance pay agreement.

text.p: Venezuelan government, union and private sector leaders on Monday signed an historic agreement to reform the country's severance payment system, opening the way for a wider reform of the country's decaying social security system.

"This is a conceptual agreement, with some details still missing ... that lays the basis for a modern social security system in Venezuela," Planning Minister Teodoro Petkoff said at Miraflores presidential palace before the ceremonial signing.
The agreement, hammered out over the weekend, still has to be passed by Congress.
"This act is of great importance, I'm sure it will be well received," said President Rafael Caldera after the signing. "We'll send it to congress to be passed there as quickly as possible."
The agreement eliminates a retroactivity clause which meant annual severance payments were calculated based on an employee's most recent wage, so impeding wage rises.
Its approval is expected to mark the beginning of a freeing- up of Venezuela's rigid labor markets.
"Both labor and business know that Venezuela has to win the competitiveness battle," Caldera said.

Leading business chamber Fedecamaras president Jorge Serrano and union leader Frederico Ramirez Leon, president of Venezuela's largest trade union, the Confederation of Venezuelan Workers, welcomed the agreement with stirring speeches that played to their respective galleries.
"I'm sure Congress will approve it, I have no doubt," Ramirez Leon said, adding that "labor has lost nothing, given away nothing, with this."
Petkoff said the agreement added to Venezuelan Agenda's package of macroeconomic reforms and that it would ensure that the macroeconomic disequilibria of the past did not re-emerge.
"It's a huge step in the making of a modern Venezuela," he said, after reading out the document agreed-on during the tripartite talks.
- Tripartite commission remains in place to judge on labor issues

- Past severance payments, or prestaciones, will be paid on the basis of one month's salary per year worked. An additional compensatory bonus will also be paid for each year worked, up to a limit of seven years and a limit of 200,000 bolivars
- Twenty five percent must be paid within six months, with the balance paid within five years.

- Looking ahead, workers will be paid -- annually, in a manner of their own choosing -- 45 days' salary for the first year worked. Workers will also be paid 60 days for the second year and two days for each subsequent year, up to a limit of 90 days.
- The tripartite commission will rule on a new minimum wage within 30 days after the bill is made law.
